newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch- May 6.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch- May 6.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Tuesday morning:

** Indian Finance Minister P. Chidambaram is due to hold discussions with left-wing coalition partners on their demands for changes to his pathbreaking 1997/98 (April-March) budget, party officials said on Monday.
The talks are expected to be held later on Tuesday, Communist Party of India (CPI) officials, told Reuters.
The budget, widely hailed by domestic industry and foreign investors, was unveiled by Chidambaram on February 28.

** The white paper on subsidies current being circulated among Parliamentarians for debate puts the total subsidy handed out by the central and state governments at a whopping 15 percent of the gross domestic product, the Economic Times newspaper reports.
In absolute terms, this would translate to about 1,850 billion rupees, the paper says.
** High capital gains and low tax provisions helped the Industrial Credit and Investment Corporation of India (ICICI) post a higher than expected 1996/97 (April-March) net profit, analysts said.
Earlier this year, ICICI - India's second largest term-lender merged with another term-lender, SCICI, in a deal that took effect from April 1, 1996.
ICICI announced on Monday its post-merger net profit surged 62 percent to 7.7 billion rupees, outperforming analysts expectations of around 6.6-6.7 billion.

** Low global aluminium prices and a power shortage due to a grid failure lowered the net of leading private aluminium maker Hindalco Industries in the financial year ended March 31, 1997, analysts said.
Hindalco said its 1996/97 (April-March) net profit slipped to 3.91 billion rupees, from 4.01 billion rupees. Net sales fell to 11.57 billion rupees from 12.52 billion in 1995/96.
